outcome: Adverse maternal outcome (death, hospitalization due to decompensated heart failure, worsening cardiovascular status during pregnancy)
Adverse fetal outcomes (miscarriages, termination of pregnancy, fetal growth restriction (FGR), placental insufficiency, live birth rate, babies discharged alive)
Obstetric complications (complications related to mode of delivery, antepartum hemorrhage, postpartum hemorrhage, preeclampsia)
cohort: Women with acquired or congenital cardiomyopathy who were followed up or delivered at King Faisal Specialist Hospital and Research Center between January 2004 and March 2020.
finding: Women with a lower ejection fraction (≤ 30%) experienced worse fetal and neonatal outcomes, including a lower live birth rate, fewer babies discharged alive, and lower gestational age at delivery, while maternal outcomes were similar regardless of the EF level.
mod_finding: Women with a lower ejection fraction tended to deliver through a means other than simple vaginal delivery.
